title: Study evaluating the effect of ARTENSIUM® cream on knee osteoarthritis pain.
official: An exploratory double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the effect of ARTENSIUM® cream in the relief of pain in patients with knee osteoarthritis
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the specific therapeutic effect of ARTENSIUM® cream compared with placebo on pain in patients with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis after 7 and 14 days of treatment.
conditions: Knee osteoarthritis is a chronic degenerative joint disease characterised by progressive deterioration of the articular cartilage and structural changes affecting the entire joint. Patients commonly experience knee pain, stiffness, reduced physical function and impaired quality of life. This study focuses on adults with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis experiencing knee pain requiring therapeutic management.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Female or male patients aged from 50 to 75 years old
2. Diagnosis of knee osteoarthritis meeting the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria, irrespective of the diagnostic modality used (clinical only, clinical-radiographic, or clinical-biological), with a knee radiograph performed within the previous 24 months
3. Mild to moderate knee pain (right or left knee) at inclusion (VAS ≥30 mm and ≤60 mm). In cases of bilateral knee involvement, the study knee (index knee) will be defined as the knee with the highest pain intensity at inclusion. In case of equal pain intensity, selection of the index knee will be left to the investigator’s discretion
4. Patient reporting a progressive increase in pain during the previous 15 days (pain greater than their usual stable condition)
5. No modification of non-pharmacological management (particularly physiotherapy) during the 3 weeks preceding inclusion. If physiotherapy is ongoing, treatment must have remained stable (same frequency and modalities) during the 3 weeks preceding inclusion
6. Patient has received and read the Information Sheet, has been given sufficient time to ask questions, and has voluntarily signed the informed consent form
7. Patient able to comply with scheduled visits, ambulate independently (without wheelchair or walking frame), correctly administer the investigational treatment independently or with assistance, and fulfil all other study requirements
Exclusion criteria:
1. Ongoing opioid treatment at the time of inclusion, irrespective of formulation or indication
2. Knee joint effusion
3. Referred pain originating from lumbar, sacroiliac, or hip disorders
4. Active cancer at inclusion
5. Ongoing anticancer treatment, including hormonal therapies, targeted therapies, and immunotherapies, including adjuvant or maintenance treatment
6. History of surgery on the index knee within 3 months before inclusion
7. History of mesotherapy on the index knee within 3 months before inclusion
8. Acute inflammatory or infectious skin conditions: open wounds, eczema, skin rash
9. Any chronic or acute condition deemed by the investigator incompatible with study participation (e.g., neuropathic pain), or severe infection potentially compromising short-term prognosis
10. Suspected or confirmed acute infection or acute inflammatory disorder at inclusion, defined by suggestive clinical signs and/or CRP ≥3× the upper limit of normal
11. Intra-articular injection or infiltration in the index knee within 3 months before inclusion
12. Ongoing aspirin treatment at analgesic or anti-inflammatory doses. Low-dose aspirin used for antiplatelet purposes is permitted
13. Women of childbearing potential not using effective contraception, as well as pregnant or breastfeeding women
14. Known hypersensitivity to any active substance or excipient of the investigational product (particularly chlorhexidine) or placebo. A test application on a small skin area will be performed at Day 0
15. Individuals deprived of liberty or under legal protection measures in accordance with Articles L1121-6 and L1121-8 of the French Public Health Code
16. Patient not affiliated with or not benefiting from the French social security system
17. Any condition that, in the investigator’s opinion, would make participation unsuitable or prevent compliance with study requirements
18. Participation in another clinical study at the time of inclusion
19. Ongoing systemic or topical NSAID treatment that cannot be discontinued at inclusion
20. Ongoing treatment with nefopam or metamizole, irrespective of formulation or indication
21. Ongoing corticosteroid therapy, regardless of route of administration
22. Presence of a total or partial prosthesis on the index knee
23. Chronic rheumatologic disease, including :  •	chronic low back pain, chronic hip pain, •	Autoimmune diseases involving the joints, including rheumatoid arthritis affecting the knee, systemic lupus erythematosus, psoriatic arthritis, and chronic inflammatory rheumatic disorders such as spondyloarthritis. •	chronic osteomyelitis of the knee joint,  •	avascular necrosis of the femur or tibia,  •	lumbo-radiculopathy,  •	bone or cartilage neoplasms,  •	metabolic diseases such as gout or Paget’s disease.  •	Chronic inflammatory crystal arthropathy due to calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystal deposition disease (systemic chondrocalcinosis). Isolated asymptomatic meniscal calcification identified on radiographic imaging is not an exclusion criterion. In case of doubt, the presence of the term “chondrocalcinosis” in the patient's medical records should be considered exclusionary. •	Tendinitis documented by imaging, periarticular bursitis, patellofemoral syndrome, iliotibial band syndrome, patellar or quadriceps tendinopathy
24. Acute or subacute traumatic knee injuries (<6 weeks), including sprains, meniscal lesions, swelling, or fractures
25. Septic arthritis of the knee or monoarthritis of the knee
